prompt: This is a feature article I drafted about modern analytics platforms. It's way too long and I know it's repetitive. Can you tighten it up to HBR standards? File is at editing-hbr-articles-workspace/test-article-3-bloated-redundant.md

assertions.text: Edited article word count is at least 25% less than original (~1800 words or fewer, original is ~2400)
The 'democratization' concept is stated/explained once, not restated 3-4 times across the article
No more than 5 instances of passive voice constructions ('is being transformed by', 'was being adopted', etc.)
Final section does not repeat 'three fundamental ways' or re-summarize the article's main points from the intro
Editorial summary includes before/after word count with percentage reduction
